summary: An informational memo defining the initial assignment of IPv6 multicast addresses.

plainLanguage.summary: RFC 2375 is a list of IPv6 multicast group addresses. Each line gives one address and says what it is for, such as all routers on a link, or the servers that answer a time request.

subtitle: The registry of reserved IPv6 multicast group addresses and their purposes.

tldr.problem: IPv6 multicast lets one sender deliver a packet to many receivers at once by addressing a group rather than individual hosts, and the Internet needs a shared registry so that two services do not claim the same group address.
tldr.mechanism: RFC 2375 defines the initial allocations of the multicast address space: node-local groups for essential protocols, link-local groups such as the OSPF and DHCPv6 agent groups, site-local groups, and globally scoped groups for services such as NTP and multimedia conferences.
tldr.outcome: It is an Informational registry that adapts the IPv4 multicast assignments, and it says the rules for assigning new addresses live in the IPv6 Addressing Architecture. The Security Considerations section says it does not directly affect the security of the Internet.

facts.label: Valid at any scope
facts.value: FF0X::/8, with X for any legal scope value

today: RFC 2375 is an Informational memo from July 1998, and the metadata records no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. It defines the initial assignment of IPv6 multicast addresses, and its Security Considerations section says it does not directly affect the security of the Internet infrastructure or its applications.

sections.title: What This Document Assigns
sections.content:
This document defines the initial assignment of IPv6 multicast addresses. It is based on the IP Version 6 Addressing Architecture and on the current IPv4 multicast address assignments, and it adapts the IPv4 assignments that are relevant to IPv6. IPv4 assignments that were not relevant were not converted into IPv6 assignments, and comments are solicited on that conversion. All other IPv6 multicast addresses are reserved.

The memo points readers to two other documents. Sections 2 and 3 specify the reserved and preassigned IPv6 multicast addresses, while the Addressing Architecture defines the rules for assigning new IPv6 multicast addresses. The key words MUST, MUST NOT, REQUIRED, SHALL, SHALL NOT, SHOULD, SHOULD NOT, RECOMMENDED, MAY and OPTIONAL are used as described in RFC 2119.
sections.plainLanguage: The list is built by copying the IPv4 multicast registry and keeping the entries that make sense for IPv6. The rest of the address space is left free for later.

sections.title: Fixed Scope Multicast Addresses
sections.content:
These are permanently assigned multicast addresses that are valid over a specified scope value. The first group is the node-local scope, where the group is confined to a single node: FF01:0:0:0:0:0:0:1 is the All Nodes Address and FF01:0:0:0:0:0:0:2 is the All Routers Address.

The link-local scope covers the addresses that matter only on one link. The list holds the All Nodes Address at FF02:0:0:0:0:0:0:1 and the All Routers Address at FF02:0:0:0:0:0:0:2, with FF02:0:0:0:0:0:0:3 left unassigned. Then come the addresses used by routing and management protocols: DVMRP Routers at FF02:0:0:0:0:0:0:4, OSPFIGP at FF02:0:0:0:0:0:0:5, OSPFIGP Designated Routers at FF02:0:0:0:0:0:0:6, ST Routers at FF02:0:0:0:0:0:0:7, ST Hosts at FF02:0:0:0:0:0:0:8, RIP Routers at FF02:0:0:0:0:0:0:9, EIGRP Routers at FF02:0:0:0:0:0:0:A, Mobile-Agents at FF02:0:0:0:0:0:0:B, All PIM Routers at FF02:0:0:0:0:0:0:D and RSVP-ENCAPSULATION at FF02:0:0:0:0:0:0:E. There are also the Link Name address at FF02:0:0:0:0:0:1:1 and All-dhcp-agents at FF02:0:0:0:0:0:1:2. The last entry of this scope is the Solicited-Node Address, FF02:0:0:0:0:0:1:FFXX:XXXX.

The site-local scope holds the All Routers Address at FF05:0:0:0:0:0:0:2, All-dhcp-servers at FF05:0:0:0:0:0:1:3, All-dhcp-relays at FF05:0:0:0:0:0:1:4 and Service Location at FF05:0:0:0:0:0:1:1000.
sections.plainLanguage: Some groups only make sense inside one machine, some only on one cable, and some inside one site. The memo gives each of those its own block of addresses, so a router on a link never sees traffic meant for a whole site.

sections.title: All-Scope Multicast Addresses
sections.content:
The second family of permanently assigned addresses is valid over all scope ranges. The memo shows this with an X in the scope field of the address, meaning any legal scope value, so the addresses are written as FF0X:0:0:0:0:0:0:0 and so on.

One rule matters for anyone using these groups: as defined in the Addressing Architecture, IPv6 multicast addresses that differ only in scope represent different groups, and nodes must join each group individually. The same service is therefore a different group at each scope.

The registry itself begins with the Reserved Multicast Address at FF0X:0:0:0:0:0:0:0 and then lists services carried over from IPv4: the VMTP Managers Group at FF0X:0:0:0:0:0:0:100, the Network Time Protocol at FF0X:0:0:0:0:0:0:101, SGI-Dogfight at 102, Rwhod at 103, VNP at 104, Artificial Horizons - Aviator at 105, NSS - Name Service Server at 106, AUDIONEWS - Audio News Multicast at 107, SUN NIS+ Information Service at 108, MTP Multicast Transport Protocol at 109, the IETF audio and video groups from 10A to 10F, MUSIC-SERVICE at 110, the SEANET telemetry and image groups at 111 and 112, MLOADD at 113, any private experiment at 114, DVMRP on MOSPF at 115, SVRLOC at 116, XINGTV at 117, microsoft-ds at 118, the nbc-pro and nbc-pfn groups at 119 and 11A, the lmsc-calren groups from 11B to 11E, ampr-info at 11F, mtrace at 120, the RSVP-encap groups at 121 and 122, SVRLOC-DA at 123, rln-server at 124, proshare-mc at 125, dantz at 126, the cisco-rp groups at 127 and 128, gatekeeper at 129, iberiagames at 12A, the unofficial BSD rwho group at 201 and SUN RPC PMAPPROC_CALLIT at 202.

The list finishes with ranges rather than single addresses. Multimedia Conference Calls run from FF0X:0:0:0:0:0:2:0000 to FF0X:0:0:0:0:0:2:7FFD, SAPv1 Announcements sit at FF0X:0:0:0:0:0:2:7FFE, SAPv0 Announcements, marked deprecated, at FF0X:0:0:0:0:0:2:7FFF, and SAP Dynamic Assignments run from FF0X:0:0:0:0:0:2:8000 to FF0X:0:0:0:0:0:2:FFFF. Every entry in the list carries the name of the person or document behind it.
sections.plainLanguage: These groups work at any size, from one machine to the whole Internet. A group that is used at two different sizes is still two different groups, so a host has to join each one it wants.

sections.title: Security Considerations
sections.content: The memo says it defines the initial assignment of IPv6 multicast addresses, and that as such it does not directly impact the security of the Internet infrastructure or its applications.
sections.plainLanguage: Assigning numbers does not make anything more or less secure, and the memo says so.
